items.title: Root cause analysis via difference graph discovery from linear time-series data
items.abstract: Root cause analysis aims to identify the mechanisms responsible for anomalies in complex dynamical systems. In this paper, we study root cause analysis in linear time-series through the lens of difference graph discovery. We focus on effect-defying root causes, corresponding to variables whose causal coefficients change between a normal and an anomalous regime. We formalize this problem using linear discrete-time dynamic structural causal models and adapt several methods originally introduced for discovering difference graphs between two populations to the time-series setting, where the two populations are replaced by a normal and an anomalous regime. We first evaluate the proposed approaches on simulated data, and then demonstrate their practical relevance on real-world datasets from IT monitoring and intensive care monitoring. Our results show how difference graph discovery can help localize causal mechanisms responsible for anomalous behavior.

items.title: Conditional-Independence-Regularized Distributional Autoencoders for Mixed-Type Data
items.abstract: Mixed-type data containing both numerical and categorical variables arise in many scientific and real-world applications. Existing representation learning and generative modeling approaches typically focus either on reconstruction accuracy or unconditional data generation, but often fail to recover the full conditional distribution of the data while preserving interpretable structural relationships between heterogeneous variable types. In this work, we introduce Conditional-Independence-Regularized Distributional Autoencoders, a framework for learning low-dimensional representations of mixed-type data through conditional distribution matching and structural regularization. Our method combines an energy-score-based objective for numerical variables, a likelihood-based objective for categorical variables, and an auxiliary conditional independence regularization term encouraging the learned representation to capture the dependence between numerical and categorical components. We provide theoretical analysis showing that the optimal representation balances unexplained numerical variability, conditional entropy of categorical variables, and residual conditional dependence. Empirically, the proposed method achieves strong performance on both synthetic and real-world datasets, substantially improving categorical distribution recovery, achieving competitive overall conditional distribution recovery, and preserving mixed-type dependence structure. The code has been made available at GitHub.

items.llm_tldr_en: Existing representation learning for mixed-type data often ignores conditional distributions and structural relationships. This paper proposes Conditional-Independence-Regularized Distributional Autoencoders, combining energy-score objectives with structural regularization to learn low-dimensional representations via conditional distribution matching, preserving interpretable relationships among heterogeneous variables.
items.llm_tldr_cn: 现实与科研中常出现含数值和类别变量的混合类型数据，而现有表示学习与生成方法通常只关注重构精度或无条件生成，难以恢复完整条件分布并保持变量间的可解释结构关系。为此本文提出条件独立性正则化的分布自编码器，通过能量分数目标与结构正则化进行条件分布匹配，学习低维表示。该方法在保留异质变量间结构性关系的同时提升了条件分布建模能力。该工作为表格型混合数据的表示学习提供了一种新框架。
